title: David Coleman joins the School of Dental Science
text: Coleman, a Trinity graduate, joins the School of Dental Science and goes on to lead microbiology research at the Dublin Dental Hospital for more than three decades, later becoming Professor of Oral and Applied Microbiology and Head of the Division of Oral Biosciences.

title: Derek Sullivan joins the lab
text: Derek Sullivan joins the microbiology group, beginning a long collaboration with David Coleman on the biology of Candida.

title: A new yeast species is named after Dublin
text: Derek Sullivan, David Coleman and colleagues describe Candida dubliniensis, a new species found in the mouths of people with HIV infection. It gives the lab its name.

title: Ten years of C. dubliniensis
text: Sullivan, Moran and Coleman review a decade of work showing that, although it is very closely related to C. albicans, C. dubliniensis is less virulent, and that missing or divergent genes may explain the difference.
ref_label: Sullivan, Moran & Coleman, FEMS Microbiology Letters

title: Cleaner water in the dental clinic
text: Coleman's group develops automated systems that use electrochemically activated solutions to control biofilm in dental unit waterlines, work carried into infection control across the dental clinic.

title: Tracking MRSA in Irish hospitals
text: The lab builds a long-running programme on the population biology, evolution and antibiotic resistance of MRSA, moving to whole-genome sequencing to follow new clones as they emerge.
ref_label: e.g. Earls, Kinnevey et al. 2017, PLoS ONE

title: The TLO genes encode Mediator subunits
text: Moran and Sullivan's groups show that the TLO genes of C. albicans encode subunits of Mediator that regulate distinct virulence traits, opening the lab's main line of Candida research today.

title: More TLO genes, more virulence
text: Expansion of the TLO gene family is shown to enhance the virulence of Candida species.

title: The whole TLO family deleted with CRISPR-Cas9
text: Removing the whole family reveals different roles for the α, β and γ clades. Follow-up work links the family to antifungal tolerance (2024) and shows that α-TLO genes drive virulence (2026).

title: Hidden diversity of vancomycin-resistant enterococci
text: Kinnevey, Coleman and colleagues find that 70% of patients studied in an Irish hospital carried more than one lineage of vancomycin-resistant E. faecium.
ref_label: Kavanagh, Kinnevey et al., JAC-Antimicrobial Resistance

title: A new generation
text: Following David Coleman's retirement, the lab continues as three research groups led by Gary Moran, Derek Sullivan and Peter Kinnevey, working on Candida gene regulation, fungal virulence and antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
